question: What is the smallest schema-valid document and identity contract that all editors and codecs must preserve?
trigger: The owner said "go model" after review-ledger next returned the model unit. The 2026-09-11 Pursue had landed in e0c1500b95 with no bound execution, and most of its inputs changed since.
requirements: Preserve one schema-valid immutable JSON document model with primary children, optional object metadata and named-root maps.
Every public assertion over unknown must validate the base shape it narrows to, and no ingress may silently drop or accept a field the others refuse.
One owner decides which top-level document fields are admitted, and construction, assertion, fitting, direct replacement, the persisted envelope and Plate migrations agree.
Keep runtime NodeKey, optional persisted element identity and schema lineage distinct where their lifetimes and jobs differ.
Keep neutral model law in Plite; Plate product defaults and application migrations call the Plite owner instead of copying its rules.
Assessment and recording only; no product change in this review.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-11 decision, its ownership flow and its rejected alternatives. Rechecked live: the focused regression and three adjacent test files (49 pass), a static census of every Plite and Plate document ingress, a static trace of every identity consumer changed since 2026-09-11, and a new public-API probe of unknown top-level document keys in raw and closed-schema editors.
summary: Pursue the last two gaps in the September owner's contract. The owner landed, and every Plite and Plate ingress reaches it. Nothing decides unknown top-level keys. assertDocument accepts a document with an extra field that construction, fitting and direct replacement silently strip and the persisted envelope rejects, and direct replacement even admits a non-JSON value there. Plate migrateDocument re-implements the owner's rules because the owner is not exported to Plate. Make document-shape.ts admit only children, meta and roots at every ingress, and expose it to Plate through plitejs/internal. Keep the JSON tree and the three-identity split.

callSites.current:
editor.read.schema.assertDocument({ children, extra: 1 }); // accepts
editor.update.value.replace({ children, extra: 1 }); // accepts, drops extra
editor.update.value.replace({ document: { children, extra: 1 }, schema }); // rejects
callSites.proposed:
editor.read.schema.assertDocument({ children, extra: 1 }); // rejects: unsupported document field
editor.update.value.replace({ children, extra: 1 }); // rejects; app data belongs in meta
editor.update.value.replace({ document: { children, meta: { extra: 1 } }, schema }); // accepts

reconciliation.question: What is the smallest schema-valid document and identity contract that all editors and codecs must preserve?
reconciliation.reason: Its owner, the JSON tree and the three-identity split hold. The patch landed and every ingress but Plate migrations reaches the owner; this review adds the unknown-key rule and the migrations duplicate to that same owner.

reconciliation.question: What is the smallest schema-valid document and identity contract that all editors and codecs must preserve?
reconciliation.reason: The bound execution shows the September owner adopted at construction, assertion, fitting and both replacements, which is the base this review's two gaps build on.

alternatives: Keep/configure: rejected. The September requirements say an assertion validates the base shape it narrows to and no malformed container silently disappears; the probe shows assertDocument accepting and every replacement path but the envelope stripping an unknown top-level key, and direct replacement admitting a non-JSON value there.

Change the existing owner: selected. document-shape.ts admits only children, meta and roots, so assertion, construction, fitting and both replacements agree with the persisted envelope that already refuses other fields; Plate migrations call it through plitejs/internal and assertOwnedDocument goes.

Preserve unknown top-level keys as an open document: rejected. They would form a second untyped metadata bag beside meta, outside the declared EditorDocumentValue type and invisible to history, Yjs and codecs; meta already carries application data.

Delete/merge: delete assertOwnedDocument in Plate migrations and the second persisted-envelope key check. ElementIdPlugin's commit-maintained id-to-NodeKey index and read API show no in-repo production caller (inferred from a grep); they stay a cut candidate for the plan to test with pstack:why and an external-usage check.
Add a public validated Document wrapper or parser family: rejected again; the assertion and replacement contracts already express the job.

One universal persisted identity owned by Plite: rejected again. Every durable identity job added since 2026-09-11 (authored lineage, Yjs moves, prepared transaction keys) needs text-level or transport-scoped identity an element ID cannot give, and copy and paste regenerate element IDs by design.
Move validation into Plate or codecs: rejected; raw Plite ingress must keep the same law.
proofLimits: The probe runs the public API on source with bun, with no package build, in raw and closed-schema editors: four cases through five ingress paths. The ingress census and the identity trace are static source reads, not runtime proof. That ElementIdPlugin's read API has no production caller is inferred from an in-repo grep and says nothing about external applications. No fix, typecheck, browser or performance claim. Whether any ingress legitimately needs a top-level field besides children, meta and roots is for the plan to settle.
